newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' 20-yr bond coupon seen 14.5-16 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' 20-yr bond coupon seen 14.5-16 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' maiden 20-year treasury bond on Tuesday is expected to have a coupon of between 14.5 and 16.0 percent, a Reuters poll of five bankers showed.
The Philippines' Bureau of Treasury is scheduled to auction two billion pesos worth of 20-year T-bond at 0500 gmt.
It will be the longest maturing government securities in the region.
A treasurer at one major foreign bank said he expected the coupon to be around 15.0 percent.
He said the small offering has made the bonds very attractive, though rising short-term interest rates would make some banks wary about bidding too low.
Treasury bill yields have been on the rise in the past weeks after falling to single digit levels in late March.
"Definitely, it's going to have an impact on the bidding today ... Some banks were quoting as low as 14.0 percent as late as last week," he said.
Another treasury official from a foreign bank said she believed the rate would hover at 16.0 percent due to the firmer T-bill rates.
"Anything below 15.0 percent will be too risky ... It should be between 15.0 to 15.5 percent," a treasurer of a large domestic commercial bank said.
He said the higher coupon should compensate for the long holding period for the instrument.
Ten-year T-bonds were being quoted at 13.0 percent in the secondary market.
Another treasury official from a medium-sized bank, who predicted a coupon of 15.0 to 16.0 percent, agreed.
"We should give premium to 20-year bond holders," he said, adding in the secondary market would be very tight because many of the bidders are buy-and-hold investors.
However, another trader from a major local bank predicted the coupon would hit a low of 14.5 percent.
"Given the interest of the bidders, we'll be happy if we get 14.5 percent," he said.
The government is using a Dutch auction system where the coupon will be based on the highest accepted yield-to-maturity rate. All bidders who bid lower than the coupon will buy the issue at par.
More than 40 financial institutions are expected to join the electronic bidding. -- Manila newsroom 63 2 8418938 Fax 8176267
